title: Peer Specialists Support Positive Outcomes in CoreCivic Facilities
summary: Trained peer specialists help fellow residents develop life skills and make meaningful progress toward successful reentry.
body_markdown:
In 2023, CoreCivic began piloting a peer life coaching program at Saguaro Correctional Center in Eloy, Arizona, that utilized peer specialists to support engagement, pro-social behavior and positive adjustments within correctional settings. Peer specialists are incarcerated individuals who are trained and certified to provide one-on-one and group peer support services. The goal is to promote personal responsibility, self-determination, coping skills, resilience and positive behavioral change.


The program has proven to be a great success, and that's why CoreCivic's Reentry Services team is now working to expand it to several more facilities. Matt Moore, senior director of reentry services, credits the program's success to the authenticity peer specialists bring to it.


"They have walked the walk, talked the talk, they've done the work already," Moore said. "They bring a level of expertise and credibility that we just can't."


To become a peer specialist, residents must demonstrate stability and emotional maturity, be active in programming, have a positive peer and staff reputation, and a willingness to complete the training and serve.


Moore says another benefit of peer specialist programs is that incarcerated individuals are often more responsive to their peers rather than uniformed staff or counselors, and the specialists can also help recognize triggers and behaviors that can lead to trouble.


Although the goal is for peer specialists to make a positive impact on their peers, it has been shown that participating as a peer specialist makes a big impact on the specialists as well.


“It encourages them to grow even more," Moore said. "Most specialists are people who have already been in programs, who have already been working on themselves, but this launches them to the next level of their personal growth."


In addition to the program at Saguaro Correctional Center, there is now peer specialist programming at Red Rock Correctional Center in Eloy, Arizona, and CoreCivic's Reentry Services team is working to expand to more facilities by 2027.
